chapters.summary: Council staff welcomes attendees to the New York City Council vote for the Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards, and Ethics. Staff asks that electronic devices be silenced, prohibits anyone from approaching the dais, and invites the chair to begin.
chapters.title: Committee staff opens vote meeting and sets dais rules

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to today's New York City Council vote for the Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards, and Ethics.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, we please ask that you silence all electronic devices.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At no point in time is anyone to approach the dais.

chapters.summary: Chair Sandra Ung welcomes attendees to the committee meeting and notes that she is chairing. She recognizes present members, including Council Members Lee, Encarnación, Banks, Deputy Speaker Nantasha Williams, Minority Leader David Carr, and Majority Leader Shaun Abreu.
chapters.title: Chair Sandra Ung opens meeting and recognizes committee members

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to this meeting of the Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards, and Ethics.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Council Member Sandra Ong chaired the committee.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Before we begin, I would like to recognize the other members of this committee who are present.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Council Member Lee, Akana Sion, Banks, and Deputy Speaker Natasha Williams, Minority Leader David Carr, and Majority Leader Sean Brew.

chapters.summary: Chair Ung thanks counsel to the committee Amanda DeGrasse and committee staff for preparing the hearing. She also acknowledges Chief Ethics Counsel Pearl Moore, Deputy Director Alicia Vassell, and additional attorneys in the Office of the General Counsel.
chapters.title: Chair Ung acknowledges committee counsel and public integrity staff

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: I'd also like to acknowledge the counsel to the committee, Amanda DeGrasse, and the committee staff that worked on today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Chief Ethics Counsel and Director of Public Integrity Unit, Pearl Moore, Deputy Director of Public Integrity Unit, Alicia Vassell, and the additional attorneys in the Office of the General Counsel who helped to prepare this hearing.

chapters.summary: Chair Ung says the committee is voting on six items heard on November 9, 2026. The items include a resolution approving M-100, Martha King's appointment to the Board of Correction, and resolutions approving M93, M94, M95, M96, and M97.
chapters.title: Chair Ung lists six items before committee for vote

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Today, we are voting on six items that this committee heard on November 9, 2026.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: We are voting on a resolution to approve M-100, appointment of Martha King to the Board of Corrections.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: We are also voting on a resolution

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: to approve M93, M94, M95, M96, and M97.

chapters.summary: Chair Ung explains the mayoral request under the City Charter for Council advice and consent on reappointments of Anthony Crowell and Kenneth Knuckles and appointments of Margaret Anadu and Meenakshi Srinivasan. She also notes the Mayor withdrew the candidacy of Julie Stein.
chapters.title: Chair Ung details CPC appointments and Julie Stein withdrawal

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Mayor Zahra Madani's request pushed into Section 192 of the New York City Charter.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: For the Council's advice and consent regarding the reappointment of Anthony Cromwell and Kenneth Knuckles, as well as the appointment of Margaret Anadu and Manakshi

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Shishri Navasan, the Mayor has sent over a communication withdrawing the candidacy of Julie Stein.

chapters.summary: Chair Ung asks the clerk to call the roll. Clerk William Martin identifies himself, states that all items are coupled, and records ayes from members as names are called, including Chair Ung, Riley, Abreu, Krishnan, Lee, Williams, Banks, and Encarnación before reaching Carr.
chapters.title: Clerk William Martin calls roll on coupled items

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: William Martin, committee clerk, roll call vote committee on rules, privileges, elections, standards, and ethics.

chapters.summary: Council Member David Carr asks permission to explain his vote. He discloses that Anthony Crowell, the M93 appointee, is Dean of New York Law School and that he is associated with the school; he abstains on M93 out of caution and votes no on all other items.
chapters.title: Carr discloses NY Law School tie and abstains on M93

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: I'd just like to disclose on the record of these proceedings that Anthony Crowell, with appointment M93, is the Dean of New York Law School, and I am associated with that entity.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: And I believe that out of an abundance of caution that I'm going to respectfully abstain on that particular appointment.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: I think Anthony Crowell is an excellent appointee to the City Planning Commission and has been since 2022.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: But I think, again, out of an abundance of caution and not wanting the process to be distracted because of my enrollment in a law school that he happens to lead, I will respectfully abstain on M93 and I'll vote no on all the others.

chapters.summary: The clerk announces an initial tally of seven affirmative, one negative, and no abstentions, with all items adopted. M93 is reported as adopted with seven affirmative, zero negative, and one abstention.
chapters.title: Committee reports initial adoption of all items; M93 has one abstention

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: So with a vote of seven in the affirmative, one of the negative and no abstentions, all items are adopted with M93 being adopted by the committee with seven in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and one abstention.

chapters.summary: Chair Ung says she will keep the vote open, and the clerk acknowledges. The open vote allows Council Member Kevin Riley to cast a late vote.
chapters.title: Chair Ung keeps vote open for Council Member Riley

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: I will still keep the vote open.

chapters.summary: The clerk calls Council Member Kevin Riley, who votes aye. The clerk thanks him and proceeds to the final vote.
chapters.title: Council Member Riley casts late aye

chapters.summary: The clerk reports the final vote: eight affirmative, one negative, and no abstentions on all items. For M93, the vote is eight affirmative, zero negative, and one abstention; the clerk tells the chair that this is a full committee.
chapters.title: Committee announces final vote: all items adopted, M93 abstention

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: All items have a vote of eight in the affirmative, one in the negative, no abstention, with M93.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Eight in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and one abstention.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Madam Chair, that is a full committee.

chapters.summary: Chair Ung thanks the committee and declares the meeting adjourned. The meeting ends at approximately 4:56.
chapters.title: Chair Ung adjourns the meeting

summary: Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards and Ethics held a vote meeting chaired by Sandra Ung on November 19, 2026.
The committee considered six items: Martha King's appointment to the Board of Correction and mayoral communications M93-M97 for City Planning Commission appointments and reappointments.
All items were adopted; David Carr abstained on M93 due to a disclosed NY Law School affiliation and voted no on the others, and Kevin Riley cast a late aye.
title: Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards and Ethics
